whyWeCarry: We carry Zumbador Reposado to offer guests an easy step up into barrel-rested tequila. Aging in oak barrels imparts gentle vanilla and caramel sweetness over roasted agave. It works nicely neat over ice or in stirred drinks.
seanShort: Smooth caramel and light oak resting at a great value.
notes: I pick up soft caramel, subtle toasted oak, and sweet agave on the palate. A well-rounded, easy sipper.

whyShort: Draft inventory record pending source review.
caskDetails: Charred American white oak barrels (min. 12 months)
productionMethod: Masonry oven cooked, roller mill extracted, double pot distilled
servingSuggestion: Neat in a snifter
whyWeCarry: We carry Zumbador Añejo for guests seeking smooth, aged barrel character in their agave. Extended time in charred oak barrels yields notes of dark vanilla, baking spice, and toffee. It is a satisfying after-dinner pour.
seanShort: Rich oak tannins and dark vanilla, built for sipping.
notes: I find toasted oak, dark vanilla, and gentle baking spice wrapping around an earthy agave core. Warm and smooth.

whyShort: California single malt finished in house-made umeshu casks, built for the Japanese-style highball.
caskDetails: Ex-bourbon and French oak wine casks, finished in house-made Umeshu (Japanese plum liqueur) casks
productionMethod: Pot-distilled in custom copper alembic stills, filtered through maple charcoal
servingSuggestion: In a Japanese-style Highball with chilled club soda and a lemon peel
whyWeCarry: Few American single malts carry a hook this distinct: St. George finishes Baller in casks from its own umeshu plum liqueur, layering mango, lychee and plum over a whisper of maple-charcoal smoke. It is approachable enough to win over wine drinkers yet made by one of the country's oldest and most respected craft distilleries, and it was purpose-built for the highball, making it an easy, conversation-starting pour.
seanShort: Umeshu-cask finished and built for a Tokyo-style highball.
notes: I get bright Japanese plum and tropical mango on entry, trailing into a delicate, dry maple-charcoal smoke. It makes one of the best highballs you will ever drink.

style: American Whiskey · Corn-forward · Chardonnay Cask Finished
whyShort: A light corn-forward American whiskey finished in Chardonnay barrels for buttery-oak and crisp-apple character.
caskDetails: New charred oak barrels, finished in French oak Chardonnay wine casks
productionMethod: Column and pot distilled, married and finished in wine barrels
servingSuggestion: Neat or over a single ice cube
whyWeCarry: A softer, wine-finished American whiskey that offers an approachable, low-proof alternative for guests curious about cask-finished spirits.
seanShort: Chardonnay-cask finished corn whiskey from Philadelphia.
notes: I taste crisp green apple and rich toasted brioche, followed by a buttery, vanilla-laced oak finish. Very soft and easygoing on the palate.

displayName: St. George Spirits Breaking & Entering American Whiskey
style: Blended American Whiskey · Sourced bourbon & rye + house malt · Four-grain
distilleryName: St. George Spirits (blended in-house; component whiskeys sourced)
whyShort: A four-grain blend of sourced bourbon and rye married with St. George's own California malt whiskey.
mashBill: Four-Grain blend: Corn, Rye, Wheat, and Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American oak and used cooperage
productionMethod: Master blend of sourced straight bourbons, ryes, and in-house pot-distilled California single malt
servingSuggestion: Neat, on the rocks, or in a classic Old Fashioned
whyWeCarry: A characterful, approachable blended American whiskey from one of California's pioneering craft distilleries, offering a transparent, well-composed pour at an easygoing 86 proof.
seanShort: Craft blending at its best—bourbon, rye, and house single malt.
notes: I find rich toffee and candied orange peel up front, with a lively kick of cinnamon rye and bready malt tying the finish together.

style: Irish American Blended Whiskey · Higher-Proof · Cocktail-Built
distilleryName: Blended at Wigle Whiskey, Pittsburgh (PA rye); Irish grain & pot still whiskey sourced in Ireland
whyShort: The 90-proof, rye-forward Irish-American blend built for cocktails.
mashBill: Blend of Irish Triple-Distilled Malted/Unmalted Barley & Grain Whiskeys and Pennsylvania Straight Rye (68% Rye · 18% Wheat · 14% Malted Barley)
caskDetails: Ex-bourbon barrels and new charred oak
productionMethod: Triple-distilled Irish pot still and grain whiskeys married with pot-distilled Pennsylvania straight rye
servingSuggestion: As a neat pour alongside a beer, or in an elevated cocktail
whyWeCarry: A higher-proof, spice-driven Irish-American blend that stands up in stirred and shaken drinks where a softer flagship would wash out, with a genuinely distinctive triple-distilled-Irish-meets-Pennsylvania-rye backbone.
seanShort: Triple-distilled Irish smoothness meets bold Pennsylvania rye.
notes: I get smooth vanilla cream and orchard fruit on entry, which quickly gives way to a bold, peppery Pennsylvania rye spine. Clean and punchy.

whyShort: A light, 80-proof American blended whiskey built for easy mixing.
mashBill: Blend of 25% straight whiskeys and 75% neutral grain spirits
caskDetails: Oak seasoned casks
productionMethod: Continuous column distilled and blended for lightness
servingSuggestion: In a 7 & 7 with 7UP and fresh lemon
whyWeCarry: We keep Seagram's 7 on hand because it is an indelible part of American highball history. It is light, easygoing, and unpretentious, made specifically to blend smoothly with ginger ale or lemon-lime soda. It gives guests a classic, familiar call without any fuss.
seanShort: The classic 7&7 anchor—light, sweet, and built for mixing.
notes: I get soft vanilla, sweet grain, and a touch of light honey on the nose. It goes down smoothly with zero burn and mixes cleanly into highballs.

expression: Kentucky Straight Bourbon Finished in Port Wine Barrels
ageText: No age statement (base bourbon aged ~4-6 years)
whyShort: Flagship port-finished Kentucky straight bourbon at 86.6 proof.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak, finished 4-6 months in 60-year-old Portuguese Ruby Port wine casks
productionMethod: Column distilled with copper pot doubler, batch finished in imported port barrels
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a single large cube
whyWeCarry: This is the bottle that made port-cask finishing mainstream in American whiskey, and it remains the world's best-selling ultra-premium bourbon by volume, so it does double duty as a familiar name and a genuine conversation piece. The ruby-port finish gives approachable bourbon drinkers a soft, fruit-forward sweetness at an easygoing 86.6 proof, making it an easy neat pour or a distinctive Old Fashioned base. Founder-led provenance from Louisville's first downtown distillery since Prohibition adds a story worth telling at the rail.
seanShort: Ruby port finishing that turns bourbon into liquid dessert.
notes: As someone with a background in winemaking, I love what ruby port barrels do to bourbon. You get lush blackberry jam and maple syrup up front, backed by gentle vanilla and just enough oak tannin to keep it balanced.

producerName: Buffalo Trace Distillery (for Age International, Inc.)
whyShort: The bourbon that launched the single-barrel category in 1984, drawn one barrel at a time from Buffalo Trace's higher-rye Mash Bill #2 and bottled at 93 proof.
mashBill: Undisclosed (Buffalo Trace Higher-Rye Mash Bill #2, estimated ~12-15% Rye)
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char), aged exclusively in metal Rickhouse H
productionMethod: Column distilled with copper doubler, sour mash fermentation, hand-dumped single barrel
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn or rocks glass
whyWeCarry: As the bottle credited with inventing the single-barrel bourbon category in 1984, Blanton's carries genuine provenance from Buffalo Trace and a hand-numbered, one-barrel-at-a-time pour that no two barrels replicate. The higher-rye Mash Bill #2 and 93-proof strength give it a spice-and-vanilla balance that works neat or in a cocktail, while the iconic horse-stopper bottle is one of the most requested and recognizable names on any American whiskey shelf.
seanShort: The 1984 single-barrel pioneer—smooth, balanced, and iconic.
notes: I always enjoy the silky mouthfeel on this. Creamy vanilla, caramel, and soft citrus peel lead into warm nutmeg and rye spice that finishes clean and dry.

style: Small Batch · Barrel Proof · Uncut & Unfiltered
whyShort: The original uncut, unfiltered, barrel-proof bourbon — Booker Noe's namesake.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char), center-cut rackhouse maturation
productionMethod: Column distilled, pot doubler, sour mash fermented, bottled uncut and non-chill filtered straight from the barrel
servingSuggestion: Neat with a few drops of spring water to open the proof
whyWeCarry: We carry Booker's because it remains the gold standard for uncut, unfiltered, barrel-strength Kentucky bourbon. Pulled from the center cut of Beam's rackhouses, every batch delivers massive intensity, thick chewy texture, and deep charred oak. It is the pour we suggest when a guest wants pure, uncompromised barrel power.
seanShort: Uncut, unfiltered barrel proof—add a splash of water and buckle up.
notes: I find huge waves of dark brown sugar, roasted peanuts, and heavy charred oak. It hits with serious proof heat, but giving it a few drops of water unlocks incredible caramel and baking spice depth.

whyShort: Dave Scheurich's 6-year Kentucky bourbon, aged on the rickhouse top floor and bottled at an easy 86 proof.
mashBill: Undisclosed traditional Kentucky mash bill (Corn, Rye, Malted Barley)
caskDetails: New charred American white oak barrels (6 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled, selected by master distiller Dave Scheurich, slow-proofed
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: Few pours put a genuine industry legend's name at an entry-level price: Dave Scheurich spent four decades shaping American whiskey, including Woodford Reserve, before signing every Boondocks bottle himself. Six years of top-floor Kentucky aging and a gentle 86 proof make this an unintimidating, caramel-forward bourbon that welcomes newcomers while giving enthusiasts a real distiller's pedigree to talk about. It fills the approachable-yet-credible slot on a back bar without stretching a budget.
seanShort: Crafted by industry legend Dave Scheurich—rich, caramel-forward, and smooth.
notes: I get lots of buttery toffee and butterscotch up front, with sweet cherry and mild oak rounding out the finish. Extremely approachable neat.

whyShort: Frankfort's flagship low-rye bourbon: honeyed, oak-kissed and easy.
mashBill: Undisclosed (Buffalo Trace Low-Rye Mash Bill #1, estimated ~10% Rye or less)
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char)
productionMethod: Column distilled with copper doubler, aged in centuries-old brick warehouses
servingSuggestion: Neat, on the rocks, or in an Old Fashioned
whyWeCarry: Few bottles deliver this much pedigree for the money: it is the flagship of America's oldest continuously operating distillery, built on the same low-rye Mash Bill #1 that underpins cult labels like Eagle Rare and George T. Stagg. At 90 proof it is gentle enough for a newcomer's first neat pour yet balanced enough to reward a seasoned drinker, and its honey-caramel-oak profile makes it a versatile backbone for sipping and for classic cocktails alike. A crowd-pleasing benchmark bourbon that punches well above its shelf price.
seanShort: The benchmark bourbon everyone should know by heart.
notes: I always come back to this when I want a balanced, reliable pour. Brown sugar and toffee on the front, subtle orange peel in the middle, and clean vanilla oak on the finish.

whyShort: Bulleit’s ten-year bourbon: oak-forward, mature, and accessible.
caskDetails: Selected charred American white oak barrels (No. 4 char, 10 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, aged 10 full years in Kentucky rickhouses
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a single large ice cube
whyWeCarry: We carry Bulleit 10 Year to show what a full decade of charred American oak maturation does to a high-rye mash bill. The extra years in the barrel soften the peppery rye punch into rich toasted wood, dried apricot, and deep vanilla. It is an affordable, age-stated step up that excels neat or over a rock.
seanShort: Ten years of oak transforms the signature Bulleit spice.
notes: I find rich toasted oak and cinnamon upfront, followed by dried fruit and leather. That decade in wood gives it great depth without making it dry.

whyShort: Bulleit's first Bottled-in-Bond: a 7-year, 100-proof, high-rye bourbon distilled entirely in-house.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (7 years in federally bonded warehouse)
productionMethod: Single distilling season at Bulleit's Shelbyville distillery, column distilled, bottled at 100 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat or as the backbone of a spirit-forward cocktail
whyWeCarry: This is a legitimate Bottled-in-Bond bourbon at a real value price, meaning a single distillery, a single season, at least four years in a bonded warehouse, and a guaranteed 100 proof by federal law. It gives the high-rye Bulleit profile drinkers already recognize with more oak, more spice and more backbone than the standard pour, making it an easy step-up that still mixes cleanly in an Old Fashioned. As the brand's first fully self-distilled release, it also earns a spot as a talking-point bottle on any American whiskey shelf.
seanShort: 100-proof bonded power from Bulleit's own Shelbyville stills.
notes: I love the structure on this. Rich molasses and brown sugar hit first, followed by a sturdy wave of black pepper and toasted walnut that hangs on through the finish.

whyShort: High-rye Kentucky bourbon, bold and spicy at 90 proof.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, proprietary yeast strains, high-rye fermentation
servingSuggestion: On the rocks or in a classic high-spice cocktail
whyWeCarry: Its unusually high 28% rye mash gives a bold, peppery spine that most bourbons lack, so it holds its own in an Old Fashioned yet still drinks smooth neat. At 90 proof with sweet oak, maple and nutmeg leading into a long, dry finish, it delivers real backbone at an approachable price - a versatile pour that mixes and sips with equal ease.
seanShort: The high-rye standard that holds up against anything in a glass.
notes: I get dry oak, peppery rye, and nutmeg right away, with just enough sweet corn and maple to soften the edges. Clean, dry, and dependable.

distilleryName: Sourced Kentucky bourbon; bottled by Three Springs Bottling Co.
whyShort: Western Spirits' small-batch flagship: a genuine 8-year Kentucky straight bourbon, 90 proof, classic 74/18/8 mash bill, at an everyday price.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char, 8 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, aged in traditional Kentucky rickhouses, small batch selected
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a single large ice cube
whyWeCarry: A genuinely aged 8-year Kentucky straight bourbon at an everyday price, Calumet Farm's small-batch flagship over-delivers: a classic 74/18/8 mash bill, 90 proof, and heavy #4-char-barrel depth that drinks well above its shelf cost. Its thoroughbred bloodline branding, a nod to one of America's most decorated racing farms, gives it instant story on the back bar, while the rich oak, vanilla, and caramel profile makes it an easy neat pour or a dependable Old Fashioned base.
seanShort: Eight years of deep Kentucky rickhouse oak at an easy 90 proof.
notes: I find seasoned wood, vanilla bean, and toasted corn up front, trailing into a clean white pepper finish. A very polished eight-year pour.

whyShort: 6-year, 36%-rye Texas bourbon, triple pot-distilled and bottled non-chill filtered at 115 proof.
mashBill: 60% Texas Yellow Dent Corn · 36% Unmalted Rye · 4% Two-Row Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 3 char, 6 years in Texas climate)
productionMethod: Triple pot-distilled, fermented with proprietary yeast, non-chill filtered at 115 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat with a splash of cool spring water
whyWeCarry: A genuine Texas-distilled straight bourbon is a rarity on most back bars, and this one earns the slot: a 36% unmalted-rye mash bill and full pot-still production give it a peppery spine and a creamy, almost chewy body that column-still bourbons rarely match. At 115 proof and non-chill filtered, it holds its own neat or as the backbone of a barrel-strength Old Fashioned, and the Charles Goodnight cattleman story gives the pour a ready-made talking point.
seanShort: Pot-distilled Texas power—chewy, spicy, and 115 proof.
notes: I love the pot-still texture here. It is thick and chewy with intense peach and apricot fruit, giving way to heavy baking spice and bold Texas heat.

whyShort: An 8-year Kentucky whiskey re-barreled into fresh Level-4 char oak for a deeper, oakier second maturation.
mashBill: Undisclosed traditional Kentucky mash bill (Corn, Rye, Malted Barley)
caskDetails: Aged 7 years in used oak, then secondary-matured in fresh Level-4 char new American oak barrels
productionMethod: Column distilled with copper pot doubler, dual-barrel maturation process
servingSuggestion: Neat in a snifter or with one large clear cube
whyWeCarry: Double-oaked bourbons are one of the fastest-growing corners of the category, and this one earns its place on liquid alone: eight years of age, a second maturation in fresh Level-4 char American oak, and a 92-proof bottling that stays balanced rather than over-extracted. It carries genuine heritage too, from a brand dating to 1856 that ran through Prohibition speakeasies, poured from a striking replica apothecary bottle that reads instantly on a back bar. For a guest who likes their bourbon oaky, rich, and a little different, it is an easy and memorable step up.
seanShort: Eight years in barrel finished in fresh heavy char—rich and dark.
notes: I get dark cocoa, heavy toasted vanilla, and sweet charred oak on the nose. The second barrel gives it a luscious, dessert-like finish that lingers.

whyShort: Bottled-in-bond Kentucky straight bourbon at 100 proof, aged 4+ years from a small-cask 70/21/9 mash.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char, 4+ years in bonded warehouse)
productionMethod: Distilled in a single season at Bardstown Bourbon Co., column/pot doubler distilled, bottled at 100 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat or in a stirred classic cocktail
whyWeCarry: Bottled-in-bond is a hard-won designation — one distilling season, at least four years in a federally bonded warehouse, and a non-negotiable 100 proof — and this pour delivers all of it from a genuinely small run of casks. The 70/21/9 mash lands in a crowd-pleasing middle: caramel-and-honey sweetness carried on a dense, oak-framed body, with enough rye spice and orange-peel fruit to stay interesting neat or over a large cube. Add a documented 19th-century Kentucky pedigree and real speakeasy lore, and it reads as an approachable but serious back-bar bourbon at a fair pour price.
seanShort: Bonded 100-proof Kentucky straight bourbon with historic speakeasy roots.
notes: I find rich butterscotch and clover honey balanced by bright orange peel and toasted clove. It has great weight on the palate and a clean bonded finish.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · The Famous Old Brand
whyShort: A pre–Civil War Kentucky label that survived Prohibition in tin cans at the Cotton Club.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (5 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled with copper doubler, aged in Kentucky rickhouses
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: It carries our event history — we built February’s six-course whiskey dinner around this label — and it gives the list a real 1856 Kentucky story at an age-stated price the York market respects. Guests who were in the room that night still ask for it by name.
seanShort: “History gets a bottle on my shelf once. Liquid keeps it there. This one stayed.” — Sean
notes: We built a whole evening around this label in February — six whiskeys, six courses — and this 5 Year was the pour that surprised the room. History gets a bottle on my shelf once. Liquid keeps it there. This one stayed. Low inventory right now, so if the bartender offers it, say yes.

whyShort: A 10-year, 90-proof Buffalo Trace bourbon from low-rye Mash Bill #1, built from individually selected barrels.
mashBill: Undisclosed (Buffalo Trace Low-Rye Mash Bill #1, estimated ~10% Rye or less)
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char, aged 10 full years)
productionMethod: Column distilled with copper doubler, sour mash fermented, matured in traditional brick rickhouses
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn glass
whyWeCarry: A genuine 10-year age statement at 90 proof is a rare thing to find on a back bar at this price, and it comes from one of the most respected distilleries in Kentucky. The low-rye Mash Bill #1 delivers an approachable, oak-and-toffee profile that pleases both newcomers and seasoned bourbon drinkers, and its individually selected barrels give it real depth for a core-range pour. It sits in that sweet spot of provenance, age, and drinkability that makes it an easy recommendation neat, on the rocks, or in a spirit-forward cocktail.
seanShort: Ten years of Buffalo Trace aging—toffee, orange peel, and oak perfection.
notes: I love the orange peel and leather aromatics on this. The palate brings buttery toffee and seasoned oak that stays refined and balanced through a gentle, dry finish.

whyShort: Heaven Hill's flagship 8-12 year small-batch bourbon at 94 proof, a longtime quality-to-value benchmark.
caskDetails: Level 3 charred American white oak barrels (blend of 8 to 12-year-old stocks)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, natural limestone water, small batch blended from ~200 barrels or fewer
servingSuggestion: Neat, on the rocks, or in an Old Fashioned
whyWeCarry: Few bourbons pack this much genuine age into an everyday price: each batch is composed from barrels matured 8 to 12 years, then bottled at an approachable 94 proof. It bears the name of the man Heaven Hill calls the Father of Bourbon and has stood as a critical quality-to-value benchmark since 1986. That mix of real maturity, easy drinkability, and pedigree makes it a versatile pour that holds up neat, over a large cube, or as the backbone of an elevated cocktail.
seanShort: The 94-proof benchmark for small-batch Kentucky oak.
notes: I always admire the oak depth here. Warm vanilla, nutmeg, and charred barrel char hit upfront, balanced by a round caramel sweetness that lingers.

whyShort: Grain-to-glass Evanston straight bourbon: corn-sweet, rye-spiced, dry oak finish at 46.5% ABV.
mashBill: 70% Corn · 20% Northern Rye · 10% Two-Row Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred Minnesota American oak barrels (char #3)
productionMethod: Grain-to-glass, fermented with French wine yeast, custom copper pot/column hybrid distilled
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks with an orange swath
whyWeCarry: This is a genuine grain-to-glass craft bourbon, milled and distilled in-house on a high-rye three-grain mash that gives it far more spice and structure than the usual corn-forward pour. Aged in tight-grained Minnesota oak, it lands a dry, peppery, caramel-and-oak profile at an approachable 93 proof that drinks well neat or as the backbone of a bolder Old Fashioned. Its origin story, craft whiskey born in the historic heart of the American temperance movement, gives it a talking point few bottles on the shelf can match.
seanShort: Bold, grain-to-glass high-rye bourbon born in Evanston.
notes: I taste lots of spicy black pepper and clove right away, wrapped in tight Minnesota oak tannins with sweet caramel corn underpinning the mid-palate.

whyShort: A 100-proof, 7-year bonded bourbon meeting the strict 1897 Bottled-in-Bond standard, from family-owned Heaven Hill.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char, aged 7 years in bonded rickhouses)
productionMethod: Distilled in a single season at Bernheim Distillery (DSP-KY-1), column distilled with copper doubler, bottled at 100 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a splash of spring water
whyWeCarry: Few bottles pack this much provenance and proof into so accessible a pour: a genuine Bottled-in-Bond bourbon that meets the exacting 1897 federal standard of a single distillery, single distilling season, and a full 100 proof. Aged seven years and built on the namesake recipe Heaven Hill first bottled in 1939, it delivers real oak, caramel, and rye-spice complexity that punches above its price. It is a category cornerstone that rewards curious drinkers and satisfies bonded-bourbon purists alike.
seanShort: Seven years, 100 proof, and family-owned Kentucky distilling at its finest.
notes: I get rich caramel, warm honeycomb, and seasoned rickhouse oak on entry. The 100 proof carries the spice cleanly without burning.

displayName: Horse Soldier Signature Small Batch Bourbon
whyShort: Wheated, 95-proof, non-chill-filtered small batch built for soft caramel-and-vanilla richness.
mashBill: 70% Yellow Dent Corn · 20% Red Winter Wheat · 10% Two-Row Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char, 6 to 8 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot finishing, non-chill filtered, small batch married
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a single large cube
whyWeCarry: A wheated mash bill and non-chill filtration make this a soft, caramel-forward pour that reads easily to guests stepping up from an entry bourbon while still holding body at 95 proof. The provenance is genuine and rare on a back bar: it is built by the Green Beret "Horse Soldiers" of American Freedom Distillery, and the bottle glass is pressed from a mold made with steel from the World Trade Center. That combination of an approachable wheated profile and an unusually concrete story gives it a clear role as a neat-or-rocks flagship pour.
seanShort: Soft wheated caramel with an incredible American story.
notes: I find soft vanilla, dark cherry, and buttery toffee coating the palate. Non-chill filtration gives it a lush, rounded texture at 95 proof.

whyShort: A Virginia four-grain bourbon aged on the James River waterfront, made under one rule: authentic bourbon, nothing else.
mashBill: Virginia Corn · Wheat · Rye · Malted Barley (Four-Grain)
caskDetails: Charred new American oak barrels (matured across four humid Virginia summers)
productionMethod: Double pot distilled in copper alembics, non-chill filtered, James River waterfront aging
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: A Newport News original that answers the small-producer question convincingly: an all-Virginia four-grain mash bill — corn, wheat, rye and malted barley — double-distilled and matured in new oak on the James River waterfront, giving a caramel-and-vanilla core with a dry, spice-tipped finish. At 90 proof it drinks easily neat yet holds its shape stirred into a cocktail, and its true single-distillery provenance lends a bourbon list a genuine East Coast point of difference at a friendly price.
seanShort: Four-grain Virginia craft aged on the James River waterfront.
notes: I get sweet corn, toasted oak, and a lively touch of baking spice. The waterfront aging gives it a rich, caramelized character with a clean finish.

style: Virginia Straight Bourbon · Four-Grain · Honey Cask Finished
whyShort: Four-grain Virginia bourbon finished in local honey barrels for a rich, honeyed pour.
mashBill: Virginia Corn · Wheat · Rye · Malted Barley (Four-Grain)
caskDetails: New charred oak, finished in bourbon barrels seasoned with local Virginia wildflower honey
productionMethod: Double copper pot distilled, secondary cask finished with raw local honey barrels
servingSuggestion: Neat or over a large clear ice cube
whyWeCarry: A genuinely regional finish - honey casks from Virginia meaderies - gives this small-batch bourbon a distinctive sweet character that stands apart from mainstream cask-finished releases and pairs well alongside a standard Ironclad pour.
seanShort: Finished in Virginia honey casks—sweet, floral, and 101 proof.
notes: I taste raw wildflower honey and warm vanilla right up front, balanced by 101-proof warmth and toasted oak tannins. Sweet without ever feeling cloying.

whyShort: A high-wheat Virginia bourbon that drinks bright, fruity, and soft at 86 proof.
mashBill: High-Wheat Virginia Four-Grain (Corn, High Wheat, Rye, Malted Barley)
caskDetails: Charred new American oak barrels (small cooperage)
productionMethod: Double copper pot distilled, waterfront matured, small-batch blended
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: A characterful craft bourbon from a small Virginia distillery whose high-wheat recipe offers an approachable, fruit-forward alternative to bigger, oakier pours.
seanShort: High-wheat Virginia craft—soft, cocoa-laced, and easy sipping.
notes: I get bright grapefruit peel and cocoa on the nose, leading into soft caramel and vanilla on the palate. A delightfully gentle wheated pour.

ageText: No age statement (min. 4 yrs under Bottled-in-Bond Act)
whyShort: Three Jack Daniel's straight whiskeys — rye, Tennessee, and malt — blended bottled-in-bond at 100 proof.
mashBill: Blend of 60% Jack Daniel's Straight Rye (70/18/12) · 20% Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey (80/12/8) · 20% Jack Daniel's American Single Malt (100% Malted Barley)
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (min. 4 years in bonded warehouses)
productionMethod: Distilled in a single season at Jack Daniel Distillery, charcoal mellowed components, bottled at 100 proof under Bottled-in-Bond Act
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a single large ice cube
whyWeCarry: Bottled-in-bond guarantees a single distilling season, a single distillery, and a full 100 proof — a federal seal of authenticity that reads instantly to whiskey-literate guests. Blending three distinct mash bills gives it a rye-led spice and dried-fruit complexity most single-mash Tennessee whiskeys can't match, yet it stays approachable enough to pour neat or build into a cocktail. For an accessible price, it delivers a genuine talking-point pour with real provenance behind every claim.
seanShort: Rye, Tennessee whiskey, and American single malt bonded at 100 proof.
notes: I taste dark dried cherry and malted sweetness first, followed by a bold wave of rye spice and charred oak. It has layers that unfold with every sip.

distilleryName: Jefferson's (McLain & Kyne / Castle Brands, Pernod Ricard)
producerName: Jefferson's (McLain & Kyne / Castle Brands, Pernod Ricard)
ageText: NAS · blend of reportedly 6-10 yr bourbons
whyShort: A small-batch marriage of up to four Kentucky straight bourbons — the expression that launched Jefferson's.
mashBill: Undisclosed high-rye Kentucky bourbon recipe (Corn, Rye, Malted Barley)
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (blend of 6 to 10-year-old bourbons)
productionMethod: Small-batch marriage of up to four different straight bourbon whiskeys, slow proofed to 82.3 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: As the expression that launched Jefferson's, this small-batch blend earns its place on merit and story alike: a marriage of up to four Kentucky straight bourbons that drinks soft and sweet at an approachable 82.3 proof. Its high-rye backbone and gentle price make it a versatile, easy pour — welcoming to newcomers yet carrying the pedigree of one of bourbon's best-known blending houses. Few entry-level bottles fold this much narrative into the glass.
seanShort: The original gentle Kentucky small-batch blend.
notes: I find sweet maple, warm vanilla, and light toasted corn on the palate. At 82.3 proof it goes down effortlessly without a hint of harshness.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Bottled in Bond
whyShort: A bonded Jeptha Creed bourbon built on Bloody Butcher corn.
mashBill: 70% Bloody Butcher Corn · 15% Rye · 15% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char, aged 4+ years in bonded warehouse)
productionMethod: Ground-to-glass, single distilling season, double copper pot distilled, open-top fermentation
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a splash of water
whyWeCarry: We carry Jeptha Creed Bottled-in-Bond because it celebrates ground-to-glass Kentucky farming with heirloom Bloody Butcher corn. Distilled and aged under strict bonded standards at 100 proof, it provides a distinctive nutty, earthy richness unlike standard yellow-dent bourbons. It offers guests an authentic taste of heritage agriculture.
seanShort: Heirloom Bloody Butcher corn distilled to a 100-proof bonded standard.
notes: I get orange zest and toasted crème brûlée on the nose, followed by deep roasted grain and cinnamon spice. That heirloom corn gives it a uniquely rich texture.

displayName: Jeptha Creed Straight Four Grain Bourbon
whyShort: A four-grain Jeptha Creed bourbon built around Bloody Butcher corn.
mashBill: 70% Bloody Butcher Corn · 10% Two-Row Wheat · 10% Rye · 10% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char)
productionMethod: Estate-grown heirloom grain, double copper pot distilled, non-chill filtered
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: We carry Jeptha Creed Four Grain because it balances heirloom Bloody Butcher corn with wheat, rye, and malted barley. Bottled at an approachable 98 proof, the multi-grain bill layers warm baking spice and toasted nuttiness over a savory corn foundation. It provides an authentic, estate-grown alternative to mainstream four-grain whiskeys.
seanShort: Four grains anchored by heirloom red corn—nutty, rich, and balanced.
notes: I pick up toasted pecan and dark vanilla right away, trailing into nutmeg and warm rye spice on the finish. The heirloom corn adds a wonderful roasted grain depth.

whyShort: A six-year wheated Jeptha Creed bourbon with Bloody Butcher corn.
mashBill: 75% Bloody Butcher Corn · 18% Malted Wheat · 7% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (No. 4 char, 6 years)
productionMethod: Double copper pot distilled from estate-grown grains, slow proofed
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn or rocks glass
whyWeCarry: We carry Jeptha Creed 6 Year Wheated because six years of barrel aging rounds out their signature Bloody Butcher corn into a plush, dessert-forward profile. Replacing rye with wheat yields soft cinnamon bread, baked dark cherry, and honeyed almond notes. It is a smooth, easy recommendation for wheated bourbon enthusiasts.
seanShort: Six years of age turns heirloom corn and wheat into liquid cinnamon bread.
notes: I love the bakery notes here: warm cinnamon pastry, dark cherry jam, and toasted almonds. The wheat keeps the finish silky and round.

whyShort: The benchmark 80-proof, 4-year Kentucky bourbon.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (Level 4 "Alligator" char, 4 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, fermented with proprietary yeast strain dating to 1934
servingSuggestion: In a Bourbon & Ginger or classic Highball
whyWeCarry: We carry Jim Beam White Label because it is the baseline standard for Kentucky Straight Bourbon worldwide. Aged four years in charred oak, it delivers signature notes of sweet corn, vanilla, and toasty wood. It is an unpretentious, dependable pour for casual highballs and classic mixed drinks.
seanShort: The undisputed global workhorse of Kentucky bourbon.
notes: I get classic caramel corn and vanilla on the nose, followed by a light oak and peanut note on the finish. Straightforward, familiar, and easy to mix.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Single Barrel · 120 Proof
whyShort: A 120-proof, nine-year single barrel built around deep Beam oak.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (Level 4 char, 9 full years)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, single barrel selected, bottled at 120 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat with a splash of water or over a single large cube
whyWeCarry: We carry Knob Creek Single Barrel 9 Year because nine years in heavy char oak at 120 proof delivers unmatched value in the high-proof bourbon category. It offers dense waves of charred oak, roasted peanut, and dark caramel that hold up to ice or dilution. It is the ultimate pour for guests who love big, bold Kentucky power.
seanShort: Nine years of deep char at a full 120 proof—a powerhouse pour.
notes: I find huge dark brown sugar, roasted pecan, and heavy char tannins up front. A single cube softens the 120 proof and opens up rich chocolate and leather.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Small Batch · 9 yr · 100 proof
whyShort: Nine years in charred oak at a full 100 proof — dark, rich, robustly oaky bourbon.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (Level 4 char, aged 9 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, sour mash fermented, small-batch blended at 100 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat, on the rocks, or in a sturdy Old Fashioned
whyWeCarry: We carry Knob Creek 9 Year Small Batch because its genuine nine-year age statement and 100-proof strength make it one of the absolute best values on the bourbon shelf. Crafted to recreate pre-Prohibition richness, it delivers deep caramel, toasted oak, and rye spice. It serves as a benchmark sipper and a flawless Old Fashioned base.
seanShort: The benchmark 100-proof, 9-year small batch that never lets you down.
notes: I love the robust backbone here: rich maple toffee, toasted oak, and a touch of roasted peanut on the mid-palate. Sturdy and dependable.

producerName: James B. Beam Distilling Co. (Beam Suntory)
whyShort: Kentucky bourbon partly finished in wine and Sherry casks, blended by Suntory's chief blender.
caskDetails: New charred American oak, with portions finished in California red wine casks and Spanish Oloroso sherry butts
productionMethod: Distilled by Fred Noe at Beam, finished in secondary wine/sherry casks, and blended by Suntory Chief Blender Shinji Fukuyo
servingSuggestion: Neat in a snifter or in a Japanese Highball with an orange twist
whyWeCarry: A genuine bridge between two whisky worlds: a classic Kentucky Straight Bourbon handed to Suntory's chief blender for a wine- and Sherry-cask finish rarely seen at this price. It reads as bourbon first, then opens into red-fruit and grape complexity that gives sherried-Scotch and wine drinkers an easy way in. At 94 proof and a mid-shelf price, it makes an approachable, conversation-starting pour with a real story behind the bottle.
seanShort: Kentucky bourbon meets Japanese blending and Spanish sherry casks.
notes: I get ripe plum, dried fig, and sherry oak up front, supported by brown sugar and gentle rye spice. The wine cask finish adds elegance without masking the bourbon core.

style: Wheated bourbon, bottled at barrel proof
whyShort: Maker's signature wheated bourbon, bottled straight from the barrel at cask strength for an amplified, rounder profile.
mashBill: 70% Corn · 16% Soft Red Winter Wheat · 14% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (char #3, heads char #2, aged ~6-8 years)
productionMethod: Roller mill ground, open cypress fermentation, double copper pot distilled, bottled uncut straight from barrel
servingSuggestion: Neat with a splash of water to open the rich wheated sweetness
whyWeCarry: This is Maker's Mark stripped of dilution: the same soft-wheat mash bill guests already trust, bottled straight from the barrel so every batch lands somewhere around 107 to 114 proof with fuller body and deeper caramel-and-oak intensity. It rewards a splash of water at the rail, giving guests a hands-on way to taste how proof reshapes a familiar bourbon. The wheated recipe also makes it an easy, approachable pour for drinkers who find high-rye barrel-proof whiskeys too sharp.
seanShort: Maker's Mark at full barrel proof—velvety wheat with immense power.
notes: I find rich salted caramel and toasted oak coating the tongue, with soft wheat softening the cask-strength heat. A splash of water brings out bright cherry and toffee.

whyShort: The original red-wax wheated bourbon: soft, sweet and endlessly recognizable at 90 proof.
mashBill: 70% Corn · 16% Soft Red Winter Wheat · 14% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (char #3, barrel heads char #2, aged ~6-7 years)
productionMethod: Open cypress vat fermentation with heirloom yeast strain, double copper pot distillation, hand-dipped red wax
servingSuggestion: On the rocks or in an approachable Old Fashioned
whyWeCarry: We carry Maker's Mark because it is the quintessential wheated bourbon that redefined American whiskey smoothness. Replacing the traditional spicy rye grain with soft red winter wheat creates an approachable, round profile of caramel, vanilla, and gentle oak. It is the gold standard for easy sipping and versatile cocktails.
seanShort: The red-wax wheated classic that made bourbon accessible to everyone.
notes: I get sweet vanilla frosting and soft caramel on the nose, followed by gentle wheat and toasted oak. It goes down with zero bite.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Wheated · French Oak Stave Finished
whyShort: The soft wheated Maker's base amped up with seared French oak staves for extra depth and spice.
mashBill: 70% Corn · 16% Soft Red Winter Wheat · 14% Malted Barley
caskDetails: Standard Maker's matured in new charred oak, finished 9 weeks in limestone cellars with 10 seared virgin French oak staves (Stave Profile No. 46)
productionMethod: Cypress vat fermented, pot distilled, cold-cellar secondary stave finishing, bottled at 94 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat or over a large cube
whyWeCarry: A widely respected, approachable wheated bourbon that shows how stave finishing can add oak and spice complexity without heat, making it an easy step up for Maker's Mark fans.
seanShort: Seared French oak staves bring rich baking spice to soft wheated bourbon.
notes: I love how the French oak staves transform the soft wheated base. You get toasted caramel, clove, and cinnamon spice with an elegant, lingering wood finish.

whyShort: A gently proofed, corn-forward Kentucky straight bourbon built on low-and-slow production: small batches, a low entry proof, and long-seasoned oak.
mashBill: Undisclosed corn-forward Kentucky mash bill (Corn, Rye, Malted Barley)
caskDetails: Fire-toasted then charred new American white oak barrels (18-36 month air-seasoned wood)
productionMethod: Low barrel-entry proof (103 proof), heat-cycled rickhouses, small batches limited to 20 barrels or fewer
servingSuggestion: Neat in a rocks glass or with a single cube
whyWeCarry: Michter's US*1 is one of the most recognized names in premium bourbon, and its 91.4-proof, corn-forward profile makes it an easy, crowd-pleasing pour that still rewards attention with caramel, vanilla, and stone-fruit depth. The production story gives a genuine, credible thing to talk about: small batches of no more than 20 barrels, a low 103 barrel-entry proof, toasted-then-charred oak, and wood air-seasoned for at least 18 months. It lands in the sweet spot of the shelf, elevated enough to signal quality yet approachable enough to move by the glass.
seanShort: Low barrel entry proof and toasted oak make this exceptionally smooth.
notes: I find rich caramel, apricot, and sweet vanilla on the palate. The 103 entry proof gives it a round, integrated mouthfeel that drinks well above its proof point.

whyShort: Ohio grain-to-glass, four-grain wheated bourbon; soft and softly sweet at 95 proof, aged 4+ years.
mashBill: Ohio Yellow Dent Corn · Soft Red Winter Wheat · Dark Pumpernickel Rye · Two-Row Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak barrels (heavy toast, No. 4 char, 4+ years)
productionMethod: Grain-to-glass, custom copper pot/column hybrid distillation, small batch blended
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: A wheated bourbon that trades bought-and-blended sourcing for genuine grain-to-glass provenance, with Ohio-grown corn, wheat, dark pumpernickel rye and barley distilled and aged under one roof. The wheat keeps it soft and approachable while the pumpernickel rye and a four-year minimum in fresh American oak add more structure than most easy-sipping wheaters, and at 95 proof it stays versatile neat or in a cocktail. It offers a well-made craft alternative to the familiar Kentucky wheated names for anyone chasing that soft, softly-sweet profile.
seanShort: Grain-to-glass Ohio wheater with rich coconut cream and caramel corn.
notes: I get sweet caramel corn and coconut cream right away, followed by subtle dark pumpernickel spice on the mid-palate. Soft, flavorful, and uniquely complex.

whyShort: Six-year Ohio four-grain bourbon finished 18–24 months in Spanish solera sherry casks — the anchor of Middle West's Double Cask Collection.
mashBill: Ohio Yellow Dent Corn · Soft Red Winter Wheat · Dark Pumpernickel Rye · Two-Row Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (minimum 4 years), finished 18-24 months in sun-blackened Spanish solera Oloroso Sherry casks
productionMethod: Grain-to-glass, hybrid pot/column distilled, multi-year secondary solera maturation program
servingSuggestion: Neat in a snifter or Glencairn
whyWeCarry: A six-year Ohio four-grain bourbon that graduates into sun-blackened Spanish solera sherry casks, it pours as a dried-fruit-and-dark-chocolate showcase and quietly demonstrates how a continuously refreshed solera finish differs from a one-and-done sherry butt. It gives a bourbon list a genuine craft-Ohio, cask-finished anchor with a story worth telling: grain-to-glass provenance, a four-grain mash, and a full six-plus years of age. At this price it reads as an approachable way to trade a guest up from standard bourbon into finished whiskey.
seanShort: Six-year bourbon aged in Spanish solera sherry casks—dense and fruit-rich.
notes: I love the continuous solera finish on this. Rich dark chocolate, stewed dates, and toasted walnut blanket the palate, finishing with sweet oak and baking spice.

pairings: Seared duck breast with cherry reduction
whyShort: A four-grain Ohio bourbon double-matured and finished in Spanish sherry casks for dried-fruit and cocoa depth.
mashBill: Ohio Yellow Dent Corn · Soft Red Winter Wheat · Dark Pumpernickel Rye · Two-Row Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American oak, finished in imported Spanish Pedro Ximénez & Oloroso sherry casks
productionMethod: Grain-to-glass, copper pot/column distilled, double-cask finished
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a single large cube
whyWeCarry: A grain-to-glass Ohio bourbon that trades big-brand sourcing for a genuinely distinctive four-grain mash and a sherry-cask finish, this pour lands squarely in the fruit-and-cocoa lane that sherry-curious drinkers chase. The sun-blackened Spanish cask work shows clearly on the palate — raisin, date and dark chocolate over charred oak — which gives a Midwest craft name real conversation value next to the usual Kentucky suspects.
seanShort: Soft wheated four-grain bourbon meets rich Spanish sherry oak.
notes: I find plum, dried fig, and cocoa powder wrapping around a warm, wheated core. The toasted oak provides great structure to a fruit-forward dram.

whyShort: A barrel-proof, single-barrel cut of New Riff's high-rye, non-chill-filtered bourbon — every bottle its own barrel.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (53-gallon barrels, No. 4 char heads, No. 4 char body, aged 4+ years)
productionMethod: Copper column distilled with copper pot doubler, sour mash fermented with Ohio River aquifer limestone water, bottled uncut and non-chill filtered
servingSuggestion: Neat with a few drops of water or over a large cube
whyWeCarry: A single-barrel, barrel-proof pour from a young Kentucky independent that has quickly become a reference point for high-rye bourbon done right. The 30% rye mash bill, non-chill-filtered bottling, and no-two-barrels-alike selection give it a spicy, characterful profile that rewards drinkers who want real backbone rather than a smoothed-out crowd-pleaser. At full barrel strength it works equally as a serious neat sipper and as a rye-forward foundation for a bold Old Fashioned.
seanShort: Non-chill-filtered single barrel power with a 30% rye backbone.
notes: I love the peppery punch on these single barrels. Butterscotch and dark berry fruit hit up front, backed by a wave of clove and rye spice that lingers for minutes.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Bottled-in-Bond · High-Rye · Non-Chill-Filtered
whyShort: A high-rye, non-chill-filtered Bottled-in-Bond bourbon at a straight 100 proof.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (53-gallon, No. 4 char, 4 years in bonded warehouse)
productionMethod: Distilled in a single season, copper column distilled with pot doubler, non-chill filtered, Bottled-in-Bond at 100 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat or in an Old Fashioned
whyWeCarry: A benchmark modern craft bourbon that delivers genuine Bottled-in-Bond credentials and a spice-forward high-rye profile at an approachable proof, making it an easy reference pour for the collection.
seanShort: The modern standard for high-rye, non-chill-filtered bonded bourbon.
notes: I get dark butterscotch, cracked black pepper, and brambly blackberry on the palate. At 100 proof it is balanced, punchy, and exceptionally clean.

whyShort: High-malt Colorado bourbon, slow-cut for a smooth, vanilla-and-caramel pour from master distiller Greg Metze.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak barrels (char #4)
productionMethod: Custom high-malt recipe created by Greg Metze, distilled at MGP and matured/slow-proofed over weeks in Colorado
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: This is an approachable, distinctly smooth bourbon that rewards curiosity: a high-malt mash bill and multi-week Slow Cut proofing give it a creamy texture and caramel-vanilla sweetness that lands easily neat or in a cocktail. Built by a four-decade master distiller in Greg Metze, it offers a recognizable name and a genuine point of difference at a friendly pour price, making it an easy recommendation for guests exploring beyond mainstream bourbon.
seanShort: High-malted barley and slow-cut proofing make this exceptionally creamy.
notes: I find malted milkshake, toasted almond, and rich vanilla on entry. The high malted barley content gives it a rounded, creamy texture that feels great on the palate.

whyShort: High-proof Whiskey Row bourbon built around Old Forester’s Prohibition-era story.
caskDetails: Heavily charred new American oak (Brown-Forman cooperage, heavy toast / char)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, batch proofed to 115 proof to replicate medicinal barrel-entry specifications
servingSuggestion: Neat with a splash of water or over a large cube
whyWeCarry: We carry Old Forester 1920 because it is arguably the most concentrated, decadent pour in the Whiskey Row series. Bottled at 115 proof to replicate the barrel strength required for medicinal whiskey during Prohibition, it bursts with dark chocolate, charred oak, and dark cherry. It is a perennial favorite for neat sipping and bold cocktails.
seanShort: The 115-proof Prohibition heavyweight—dark chocolate, cherry, and spice.
notes: I love the density of this whiskey. Thick dark caramel, roasted cocoa, and dark cherry syrup coat the palate, followed by a warm, lingering rye spice finish.

whyShort: The sweeter, double-barreled Old Forester Whiskey Row pour.
caskDetails: Matured in standard charred oak, then transferred into a second custom barrel charred to the point of incineration (char #5)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, secondary high-char barrel maturation
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn or rocks glass
whyWeCarry: We carry Old Forester 1910 because its second maturation in a heavily charred second barrel delivers incredible sweet-oak richness. Inspired by a historic 1910 distillery fire that forced whiskey into fresh barrels, it yields luscious notes of mocha, baked apple, and burnt caramel. It is an exceptional dessert-like dram.
seanShort: Twice-barreled into heavy char for sweet mocha and toffee decadence.
notes: I find rich butter toffee, marshmallow char, and spiced baked apple. It is soft, round, and remarkably sweet on the finish.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Whiskey Row Series
whyShort: A Whiskey Row bottle built around Old Forester’s original batching idea.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (composed of barrels from three distinct warehouses)
productionMethod: Column distilled with pot doubler, batched across three separate warehouses with different entry proofs and ages
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks with an orange twist
whyWeCarry: We carry Old Forester 1870 to pay homage to George Garvin Brown’s original batching process from three separate distilleries in 1870. Blending barrels from three distinct warehouses produces a soft, fruit-forward profile loaded with citrus, fresh apple, and vanilla. It is a gentle, historic entry into the Whiskey Row series.
seanShort: A three-warehouse blend honoring the first bottled bourbon in 1870.
notes: I get bright citrus peel, crisp orchard fruit, and light vanilla cream. It is light on its feet and finishes with delicate cinnamon spice.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Bottled in Bond
whyShort: Old Forester’s Bottled-in-Bond Whiskey Row expression.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (aged 4+ years in federally bonded rickhouses)
productionMethod: Distilled in a single season at one distillery, column and pot doubler distilled, bottled at exactly 100 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat or in a stirred cocktail
whyWeCarry: We carry Old Forester 1897 to commemorate the landmark passage of the U.S. Bottled-in-Bond Act of 1897. Distilled in a single season and bottled at 100 proof, it brings deep vanilla caramel, dried dark fruit, and bold cracked pepper spice. It represents authentic bonded Kentucky bourbon heritage.
seanShort: Crafted to honor the 1897 Bottled-in-Bond Act at a sturdy 100 proof.
notes: I find sweet caramel, dark raisins, and bold oak spice on entry. The 100-proof backbone carries a warm peppery finish that stays clean.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Bottled at 100 Proof
whyShort: A bold, rye-forward 100-proof Kentucky Straight Bourbon built for cocktails and neat sipping.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (char #4)
productionMethod: Column distilled with copper pot doubler, aged in heat-cycled warehouses, bottled at 100 proof
servingSuggestion: On the rocks or as the primary base for an Old Fashioned
whyWeCarry: A benchmark high-proof bourbon that punches well above its price, offering full-bodied spice and depth that hold up in a cocktail or on their own.
seanShort: The ultimate bartender's secret for rich, 100-proof cocktails.
notes: I get black cherry, rich butterscotch, and warm baking spice upfront. The 100-proof punch cuts through ice and vermouth perfectly.

whyShort: A high-rye, 100-proof bonded bourbon with a big cinnamon-and-spice backbone.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (Level 4 char, min. 4 years in bonded warehouse)
productionMethod: Distilled in a single season at Jim Beam Clermont/Boston, column and doubler distilled, 100 proof Bottled-in-Bond
servingSuggestion: Neat, on the rocks, or in a classic cocktail
whyWeCarry: A benchmark bottled-in-bond bourbon that delivers real high-rye spice and 100-proof intensity at an approachable price, making it a dependable, characterful pour and a versatile cocktail base.
seanShort: 27% high-rye mash bill bonded at 100 proof—spicy and bold.
notes: I love the cinnamon bite on this. Bold rye spice and cracked pepper jump out first, balanced by sweet corn caramel and toasted oak.

style: Four Grain Straight Bourbon · Finished in Vino de Naranja (Spanish orange wine) casks
distilleryName: MGP of Indiana (Lawrenceburg); blended and bottled at Bardstown Bourbon Company
whyShort: Penelope's four-grain bourbon finished in Spanish orange-wine casks for a candied-citrus twist.
mashBill: Four-Grain Blend: 74% Corn · 16% Wheat · 7% Rye · 3% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American oak, finished up to 12 months in Spanish Vino de Naranja (orange wine) casks
productionMethod: Column distilled at Ross & Squibb, small-batch blended and secondary finished in citrus wine barrels
servingSuggestion: Neat in a snifter or with a single clear cube
whyWeCarry: A well-made, approachable cask-finished bourbon whose orange-wine finish gives it a distinctive citrus signature that stands out on a bourbon shelf and works beautifully in cocktails.
seanShort: Finished in Spanish orange-wine casks—candied citrus and sweet spice.
notes: I get bright candied orange peel and floral honey on the nose, followed by warm caramel and cinnamon on the palate. A delightfully unique cask finish.

displayName: Penelope Project X · Oloroso Sherry Cask
style: Straight Bourbon · Four-Grain · Oloroso Sherry Cask Finish
whyShort: Penelope's four-grain bourbon reborn under an Oloroso sherry finish — dried fruit, black cherry, and gentle spice.
mashBill: Four-Grain Blend: 74% Corn · 16% Wheat · 7% Rye · 3% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American oak, finished in Spanish Oloroso Sherry butts
productionMethod: Column distilled at Ross & Squibb, married from three distinct mash bills, bottled uncut at cask strength
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn glass
whyWeCarry: A well-regarded example of sherry-finished American bourbon that bridges wheated softness with dried-fruit depth, making it an approachable pour for both bourbon drinkers and sherry-cask fans.
seanShort: Cask-strength four-grain bourbon drenched in Oloroso sherry fruit.
notes: I find rich Oloroso raisins, black cherry compote, and toasted walnut on entry. Cask strength gives it incredible richness without overpowering the palate.

style: Straight Bourbon · Four-Grain · Wheated · Non-Chill Filtered
whyShort: A softer, wheat-forward four-grain take on Penelope's MGP-sourced bourbon.
mashBill: Four-Grain Blend: 74% Corn · 16% Wheat · 7% Rye · 3% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (char #4, aged 4 to 6 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled at Ross & Squibb, blended from high-wheat bourbon batches, non-chill filtered
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks
whyWeCarry: An approachable, non-chill-filtered wheated bourbon at an accessible proof, making it an easy pour for guests exploring the softer, sweeter side of the category.
seanShort: Silky four-grain wheated bourbon with caramel apple and honey notes.
notes: I get crisp caramel apple and wildflower honey up front, followed by soft vanilla and light oak. Very smooth and easy to sip neat.

whyShort: Three mash bills blended into one barrel-proof bourbon — architecture over heat.
mashBill: Four-Grain Blend: 74% Corn · 16% Wheat · 7% Rye · 3% Malted Barley
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (char #4, aged 4 to 5 years)
productionMethod: Column distilled at Ross & Squibb, composite blend of 3 distinct mash bills, bottled uncut and non-chill filtered
servingSuggestion: Neat with a splash of water to tame the heat
whyWeCarry: In York, barrel-proof usually means a seventy-dollar ask. This delivers cask-strength complexity at a number our guests will order twice, and it anchors the value end of the bourbon flight — we pour it against the Booker’s on purpose, because the comparison sells itself.
seanShort: “The bottle I hand to bourbon drinkers who think they’ve tried everything under fifty dollars.” — Sean
notes: This is the bottle I hand to bourbon drinkers who think they've tried everything under fifty dollars. Barrel proof without the burn-for-burn's-sake. We keep it on the flight list on purpose — taste it against the Booker's and tell me the price difference makes sense.

whyShort: A wheated bourbon under the Bottled-in-Bond seal: one distillery, one season, four-plus years, exactly 100 proof, with a soft caramel-and-vanilla profile and bonded backbone.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (char #3, aged 4+ years in bonded warehouse)
productionMethod: Distilled in a single season at Lux Row Distillers, column and pot doubler distilled, 100 proof Bottled-in-Bond
servingSuggestion: Neat or on the rocks with a cherry
whyWeCarry: Bottled-in-Bond wheated bourbon is a genuinely narrow slice of the category: the federal bond seal guarantees a single distillery, a single distilling season, four years minimum in charred new oak, and a full 100 proof, all wrapped around the softer, sweeter wheated recipe rather than the usual rye. It delivers Weller-adjacent caramel-and-vanilla character with real structural backbone, and it punches above its shelf slot for anyone chasing the wheated profile without the allocation hunt. That combination of a legally guaranteed pedigree and an approachable, crowd-friendly flavor makes it an easy anchor for a value-minded bourbon lineup.
seanShort: Bonded wheated bourbon at 100 proof—approachable, soft, and sturdy.
notes: I get clover honey, brown sugar, and rich vanilla on entry. The wheat keeps it smooth, but that 100-proof bonded backbone gives it real grip.

style: Kentucky Straight Bourbon · Wheated · Small Batch
whyShort: A hand-selected, 110-proof small-batch take on Rebel's classic wheated bourbon.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (char #3, aged 4 years)
productionMethod: Column and pot doubler distilled at Lux Row, small-batch selected and proofed to a sturdy 110 proof
servingSuggestion: Neat with a splash of water or over a large cube
whyWeCarry: It offers a bold, higher-proof expression of a historic wheated mash bill at an approachable price, making it an easy pour for guests who like softer, caramel-forward bourbons with extra backbone.
seanShort: 110-proof wheated power with lush honey and dark fruit.
notes: I love the proof on this. Rich honeyed caramel, vanilla bean, and stewed cherries hit up front, finishing with a warm, velvety wood spice.

whyShort: A wheated Kentucky straight bourbon and the debut spirit from the family behind Kendall-Jackson.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (5+ years in Owensboro tile rickhouses)
productionMethod: Column distilled with copper doubler at Green River (DSP-KY-10), blended in 131-barrel batches

whyWeCarry: Built on a 21% wheat mash bill, this delivers the soft, caramel-forward sweetness that reads easily to newcomers yet holds depth for seasoned bourbon drinkers — equally at home neat or as a cocktail base. As the first spirit from the family behind Kendall-Jackson, released in a small 131-barrel Founder's Edition, it brings a genuine provenance story that rewards a second look. At five years and 94 proof it lands in an approachable, food-friendly sweet spot without thinning out.
seanShort: Wine pedigree meets Kentucky wheated bourbon—soft, rich, and elegant.
notes: I taste toasted toffee and baked peach right away, supported by silky wheat and creamy vanilla. It has a rounded, wine-maker's balance to it.

seanShort: WhistlePig's take on bourbon—100 proof with sweet maple and corn.
notes: I find sweet maple syrup and caramel corn on the front, followed by a gentle herbal tea and oak spice finish. Great structure for an Old Fashioned.

seanShort: Ten-year straight bourbon finished in custom toasted Vermont oak.
notes: I get dark brown sugar, roasted almond, and sweet aromatic cedar on the palate. The toasted barrel finish gives it a warm, campfire-like comfort.

whyShort: Brooklyn-married flagship: a 10-year straight bourbon from KY/TN/IN, blended in five-barrel batches, non-chill filtered and proofed with Rosendale mineral water at 91 proof.

caskDetails: New charred American white oak (aged 10 full years)

whyWeCarry: A genuine 10-year age statement is uncommon at this price, and the five-barrel batching keeps each run distinctive rather than uniform. Non-chill filtration and mineral-water proofing give it a rounder, more textural pour than most 91-proof bourbons, while the Brooklyn provenance and the Rosendale-mine backstory hand a bartender a genuine sense-of-place hook for guests who want more than another Kentucky label.
seanShort: Ten-year five-barrel blend proofed with Rosendale limestone water.
notes: I love the texture here. Sweet maple caramel and vanilla cream hit up front, backed by dark cherry and seasoned oak that finishes remarkably smooth.

whyShort: The brand's darker, more concentrated side — a 12-year single barrel at 99 proof, proofed with limestone-mine water and bottled one cask at a time.
mashBill: Undisclosed straight bourbon mash bill (Corn, Rye, Malted Barley)

productionMethod: Single barrel selected, non-chill filtered, proofed to 99 proof with Rosendale limestone mine mineral water
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn glass
whyWeCarry: A double-digit age statement is increasingly scarce, and this 12-year single barrel delivers the concentrated dark-fruit, caramel, and roasted-oak profile drinkers chase in far pricier bottles. Its Brooklyn provenance and signature limestone-mine water give the pour a story worth telling, while the 99-proof, non-chill-filtered build keeps it richly flavorful without overwhelming anyone new to older bourbon.
seanShort: Twelve years of single-barrel concentration at 99 proof.
notes: I get stewed blackberry, rich molasses, and heavy roasted oak right away. Proofed with mineral water, it has a wonderfully slick, satisfying finish.

seanShort: The 101-proof Kentucky legend that never disappoints.
notes: I love the spicy punch here: bold cinnamon, cracked pepper, and alligator-char oak, wrapped in vanilla toffee. A stone-cold classic.

whyWeCarry: We carry Wild Turkey 81 for guests who love the classic Russell family flavor profile—rich vanilla, sweet corn, and baking spice—in an easy-drinking, lower-proof format. Aged up to eight years in heavy char barrels, it delivers solid depth without high alcohol heat.
seanShort: Approachable 81-proof sipping from the Russell family.
notes: I get soft caramel, vanilla pudding, and mild rye spice on the tongue. It goes down easy and makes a great entry point into the Wild Turkey profile.

mashBill: Undisclosed proprietary high-rye Kentucky mash bill (Corn, Rye, Malted Barley)

servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn glass or with a single cube
whyWeCarry: One of Bardstown's most recognizable bottles, its pot-still-shaped glass decanter earns a spot on the back bar before the first pour. At 94 proof it drinks approachably while keeping character - caramel and vanilla balanced by cherry, citrus and a cinnamon-rye finish - an easy, familiar reach for bourbon drinkers. As a small batch from a family-run Kentucky house now running its own stills, it brings real provenance without a top-shelf price.
seanShort: Iconic pot-still decanter with bright cherry, citrus, and cinnamon spice.
notes: I find lemon peel, ripe red cherry, and sweet caramel up front, followed by a light floral and cinnamon finish. Elegant and approachable.

whyShort: Flagship Woodford Reserve given a second maturation in a deeply toasted, lightly charred oak barrel for extra sweet-oak richness.

productionMethod: Pot and column distilled blend, twice-barreled maturation process
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a single large cube
whyWeCarry: Double Oaked is one of the bottles that made twice-barreled bourbon mainstream: introduced in 2012 as Woodford's first permanent line extension, it takes an already well-regarded bourbon and re-barrels it in a second, deeply toasted oak cask for a dessert-forward wave of caramel, dark fruit and sweet oak. That extra-oak profile is approachable enough to win over wine drinkers and non-whiskey guests, yet distinctive enough to give bourbon regulars something they can't get from the standard pour - all from a National Historic Landmark distillery with a recognized, easy-to-sell name.
seanShort: Deeply toasted second barrel creates an ultra-rich, dessert-forward pour.
notes: I love the heavy toasted oak here. It drinks like spun sugar, dark maple syrup, and roasted hazelnuts, with almost zero burn on the finish.

whyShort: Flagship pot-still Kentucky bourbon at 90.4 proof — vanilla, toasted oak and rye spice.
caskDetails: New charred American white oak (char #4)
productionMethod: Blend of triple copper pot still whiskey from Woodford Reserve and column-distilled whiskey from Brown-Forman distillery, matured in stone rickhouses
servingSuggestion: On the rocks, neat, or in a classic cocktail
whyWeCarry: Few bottles pack this much name recognition and genuine craft credibility into an approachable pour: a small-batch Kentucky Straight Bourbon made in part with copper pot stills on the state's oldest distilling site. Its balanced 72/18/10 grain recipe and 90.4-proof profile of vanilla, toasted oak and rye spice drink easily neat, over ice, or as the backbone of a classic Old Fashioned. The label reassures newcomers while the liquid rewards guests who look a little closer.
seanShort: The classic, copper pot-distilled benchmark of Kentucky bourbon.
notes: I find rich vanilla, dried orange peel, and toasted oak right away. It is exceptionally well-balanced and makes a flawless Old Fashioned.

seanShort: The smooth, historic Canadian blend built for highballs since 1858.
notes: I get light toasted almond, soft vanilla, and a gentle rye kick. It is exceptionally light-bodied and mixes effortlessly.

It remains one of our most requested neat and mixed pours.
seanShort: Fifty whiskies blended for unmatched Canadian smoothness.
notes: I find sweet butterscotch, vanilla cream, and a hint of oak spice on the finish. Completely round, soft, and easy to sip.

seanShort: Six-year Canadian blend created in 1913—light, sweet, and classic.
notes: I get light caramel, orchard fruit, and gentle cinnamon on the nose. It drinks very light and clean with zero harshness.

servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn glass or with a single drop of water
whyWeCarry: Few bottles tell Ireland's whiskey story as completely as Green Spot: a single pot still whiskey from Midleton, bottled for a Dublin merchant house whose bonding lineage runs back to 1805. Its ex-bourbon-and-sherry maturation delivers green apple, clove and toasted oak in a balanced, food-friendly pour that rewards both newcomers and pot still devotees. As a category benchmark at a fair price, it earns a permanent place on any serious Irish shelf.
seanShort: The historic benchmark for Irish single pot still whiskey.
notes: I love the crisp green apple and orchard fruit on this. The pot still malted and unmalted barley gives it a luscious, creamy texture backed by clove and toasted oak.

whyWeCarry: We carry Jameson Original because it is the world's most iconic Irish whiskey, setting the global standard for triple-distilled smoothness. A marriage of pot still and fine grain whiskeys aged in ex-bourbon and sherry casks, it offers floral fragrance, vanilla, and subtle nuttiness. It is an essential back-bar staple.
seanShort: The global benchmark for triple-distilled Irish smoothness.
notes: I get soft floral notes, vanilla, and a hint of sweet sherry upfront. It goes down clean with zero harshness, making it effortless to sip or mix.

Its pot-still-forward blend is versatile enough to sip neat yet robust enough to carry an elevated Irish cocktail. The trusted Jameson name paired with a small-batch story gives guests an easy, confident trade-up.
seanShort: Double-charred barrels give classic Jameson rich butterscotch and oak depth.
notes: I find rich butterscotch and toasted oak dominating the palate, supported by ripe peach and warm vanilla. It is a fantastic step up for bourbon drinkers exploring Irish whiskey.

notes: I get creamy butterscotch and orchard fruit up front, followed by toasted wood and a lively touch of white pepper. Very clean and balanced.

whyWeCarry: Toki delivers genuine House of Suntory pedigree — malt and grain sourced from Yamazaki, Hakushu and Chita — at an approachable price that makes authentic Japanese whisky accessible rather than aspirational. Its light citrus-and-honey profile is a textbook highball base, giving a spirits list a versatile, crowd-pleasing entry point into the Japanese category. For guests curious about Japanese whisky without committing to a rare age-statement pour, it is an easy, well-made first step.
seanShort: The ultimate Tokyo-style highball whisky—crisp, citrusy, and refreshing.
notes: I get crisp green apple, fresh basil, and honeyed malt on the nose. Built specifically for highballs, it sparkles with club soda and a fresh lemon twist.

notes: I get black pepper, toasted cedar, and honeyed apple on the palate. That 53% rye recipe gives it great spice while retaining Woodford's signature roundness.
