whyShort: A rich, sherry-forward blended malt built on first-fill oloroso casks.
caskDetails: First-fill Spanish Oloroso Sherry seasoned butts, refill butts, and custom French oak casks
productionMethod: Master blended marriage of single malts (primarily Benrinnes, Glen Elgin, and Teaninich), non-chill filtered, natural color
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn glass or with a drop of water
whyWeCarry: A transparent, sherry-driven blended malt from a respected independent blender, it offers dessert-like richness that reads clearly for guests exploring sherried Scotch.
seanShort: Compass Box blending at its finest—first-fill Oloroso sherry decadence.
notes: I love the chocolate fudge and stewed plum depth here. The first-fill Oloroso casks give it rich color and spice without masking the malt sweetness.

style: Blended Scotch Whisky · Double Aged · Up to 40 malt and grain whiskies
whyShort: The double-aged Highland blend that set a global benchmark for smoothness.
mashBill: Blend of up to 40 Single Malt (Aberfeldy heart) and Single Grain Scotch Whiskies
caskDetails: Seasoned ex-bourbon and European oak casks (double-aged in vintage oak vats for 6 months post-blending)
productionMethod: Pot and column distilled, married together and double-aged in oak vats for seamless integration
servingSuggestion: In a classic Scotch Highball with club soda and a lemon twist
whyWeCarry: We carry Dewar's White Label because it has set the global benchmark for blended Scotch smoothness since 1899. Built around single malt from the Aberfeldy distillery and double-aged in oak casks, it offers heather honey, golden pear, and a subtle wisp of smoke. It is an enduring classic for highballs.
seanShort: Aberfeldy honeyed malt double-aged for timeless Highland smoothness.
notes: I get sweet heather honey and golden pear on entry, followed by light vanilla toffee and just a whisper of peat smoke. Very easy to enjoy.

style: Blended Scotch Whisky · NAS · Light peat
whyShort: The bold, spicy signature blend built to carry a highball or cocktail.
mashBill: Blend of up to 35 Malt and Grain Scotch Whiskies (Cardhu, Caol Ila, Cameronbridge)
caskDetails: Refill and ex-bourbon oak casks
productionMethod: Pot and continuous column distilled across Highland, Speyside, and Islay distilleries; master blended specifically for mixing
servingSuggestion: In a Highball with ginger ale or club soda
whyWeCarry: We carry Johnnie Walker Red Label because it is the world's best-selling Scotch whisky, purpose-built to deliver bold flavor in mixed drinks. Blending light whiskies from the Scottish east coast with dark, peaty whiskies from the west, it provides cracked black pepper, cinnamon spice, and a distinct smoky finish that cuts through soda.
seanShort: The world's favorite mixing Scotch—bold spice and smoky finish.
notes: I find vibrant cinnamon spice, cracked pepper, and an unmistakable touch of coastal smoke. It holds its character perfectly against ginger ale or soda.

whyShort: Scotland's only malt-and-grain distillery uses rare straight-neck stills and a triple American-oak marriage for a smooth, honeyed Highland style.
caskDetails: Matured in a combination of first-fill, second-fill, and re-charred American oak ex-bourbon casks
productionMethod: Distilled in unique straight-neck pot stills and traditional swan-neck copper pot stills, triple-cask married
servingSuggestion: Neat or with a single drop of water
whyWeCarry: An approachable, honey-and-soft-fruit Highland single malt from one of Scotland's genuinely idiosyncratic distilleries, the only one making both malt and grain whisky and running rare straight-neck stills found almost nowhere else. Its triple American-oak marriage and gentle wisp of smoke make it an easy, low-risk entry into single malt that still has a real story behind the glass, and at this price it punches well above its weight as a house pour.
seanShort: Straight-neck stills create honeyed orchard fruit with a whisper of smoke.
notes: I get golden honey, ripe pear, and a gentle wisp of peat smoke on the finish. It is smooth, balanced, and an approachable introduction to Highland single malt.

whyShort: The benchmark sherried Speyside — two oaks, some of the smallest stills in Scotland, no shortcuts.
caskDetails: Sherry-seasoned American oak and sherry-seasoned European oak casks (aged 12 years)
productionMethod: Distilled in Scotland's smallest copper pot stills, married from two distinct sherry wood types, natural color
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn glass or with a single drop of water
whyWeCarry: Every scotch shelf needs its handshake bottle — the name a guest already trusts. This is ours, and it earns the slot by being genuinely representative: real sherry seasoning, natural colour. We pour it beside the Tomatin and Glenlivet so the conversation has somewhere to go.
seanShort: “If bourbon is home base, this is the bridge across the Atlantic.” — Sean
notes: The sherry seasoning here is a wine-cellar play, and as a winemaker that's exactly why I respect it — Macallan spends more on oak than anyone in the business because they know the barrel IS the recipe. If you're a bourbon drinker who's never crossed the Atlantic, this is the bridge. Start here, then let us walk you toward the Tomatin.

whyShort: Speyside blended malt of Glenfiddich, Balvenie and Kininvie — no grain whisky — married in cask and bottled at 43% for a smooth, vanilla-and-fruit, mix-friendly Scotch.
mashBill: 100% Malted Barley (100% Blended Malt, zero grain whisky)
caskDetails: First-fill ex-bourbon American oak casks (married in tuns for up to 6 months)
productionMethod: Copper pot distilled single malts from Glenfiddich, Balvenie, and Kininvie, married in 27-cask batches
servingSuggestion: In a Penicillin or on the rocks with an orange peel
whyWeCarry: This is one of the few 100% malt blends on the shelf — three Speyside single malts from Glenfiddich, Balvenie and Kininvie married together with no grain whisky, which gives it real malt character at a price and proof built for everyday pouring. Its vanilla, honey and orchard-fruit profile sips cleanly neat yet holds up in a whisky sour or highball, making it a genuinely versatile bottle behind the bar. For a guest new to Scotch, it is one of the most approachable and forgiving entries into malt whisky.
seanShort: 100% Speyside single malts married for effortless mixing and sipping.
notes: I find bright orange peel, clover honey, and vanilla custard up front, with soft cinnamon spice on the finish. Completely smooth and approachable.

whyShort: An 80-proof value blended Scotch built for mixing.
mashBill: Blend of Scottish Malted Barley and Grain Whiskies
caskDetails: Refill oak casks (aged minimum 3 years in Scotland)
productionMethod: Pot and continuous column distilled, blended in Scotland for high-volume well utility
servingSuggestion: In a highball with soda or ginger ale
whyWeCarry: We keep Mr. Boston Blended Scotch on hand as an economical, unpretentious well option for casual scotch highballs and blended mixed drinks. It offers light honey, grain sweetness, and subtle peat smoke.
seanShort: Light honey and soft smoke built for everyday highballs.
notes: I get light malt sweetness, honey, and a quick touch of woodsmoke. Light-bodied, straightforward, and mixes easily with soda or ginger.

whyShort: The founding Speyside single malt, double-oak matured into a soft, fruit-forward flagship.
caskDetails: Double oak matured in traditional European oak and American white oak ex-bourbon casks (12 years)
productionMethod: Distilled in distinctive tall, lantern-shaped copper pot stills at Glenlivet, mineral-rich spring water from Josie's Well
servingSuggestion: Neat in a tulip glass or with a single ice cube
whyWeCarry: Few single malts carry this much category weight: The Glenlivet is the distillery that legalized Speyside whisky, and the 12 Year is its calling card. Double-oak maturation in American and European casks yields a soft, tropical-fruit profile that lands easily with newcomers while staying honest to a two-century house style. At an accessible price it earns its place as a recognizable, dependable gateway into single malt.
seanShort: The definitive Speyside single malt—fresh pineapple, vanilla, and marzipan.
notes: I love the tropical brightness here: fresh pineapple and honeysuckle lead into creamy vanilla and sweet marzipan. Completely unpeated and gentle.

style: Highland Single Malt Scotch · Triple Wood · Bourbon & Sherry Casks
whyShort: A smooth, fruit-forward Highland malt rounded out with Oloroso sherry casks.
caskDetails: Matured in ex-bourbon and traditional oak casks, finished 6–9 months in first-fill Spanish Oloroso Sherry butts (12 years total)
productionMethod: Double copper pot distilled with soft water from the Alt-na-Frith burn, married in sherry butts
servingSuggestion: Neat in a Glencairn glass or with a splash of still water
whyWeCarry: An easygoing, well-priced sherried Highland single malt that makes an accessible entry point for guests exploring Scotch beyond the peated styles.
seanShort: Twelve-year Highland single malt finished in Oloroso sherry butts.
notes: I get sweet crème caramel and crisp green apple up front, followed by dried sultanas and aromatic cedar on the finish. Balanced and approachable.

whyShort: Tomatin's unpeated Highland single malt, married from ex-bourbon and virgin oak casks — the US name for the expression sold as "Legacy" elsewhere.
caskDetails: Matured in a combination of ex-bourbon American oak casks and virgin American oak casks
productionMethod: Double copper pot distilled at high elevation in the Monadhliath Mountains, virgin-oak marriage
servingSuggestion: In a refreshing Highball with soda water and lemon peel
whyWeCarry: An approachable, budget-friendly Highland single malt that pours as an easy entry point into unpeated Scotch: soft vanilla-fudge sweetness and bright citrus-and-orchard-fruit notes make it forgiving for newcomers yet true to Tomatin's gentle house style. The virgin-oak component gives a young NAS malt more richness than its price suggests, and it fills the light, sessionable Highland slot on a back bar without demanding a peat-forward palate. As the US label for the whisky sold as Legacy elsewhere, it carries the pedigree of one of Scotland's historically largest distilleries at a genuinely accessible pour.
seanShort: Unpeated Highland malt aged in bourbon and virgin oak—bright and sweet.
notes: I find lemon candy, green apple, and creamy vanilla fudge on entry. The virgin oak gives it a pleasant sweetness with zero peat or smoke.

style: Tennessee Whiskey · Charcoal Mellowed (Lincoln County Process)
whyShort: The charcoal-mellowed black-label benchmark of Tennessee whiskey.
caskDetails: Handcrafted new charred American white oak barrels (char #4)
productionMethod: Lincoln County Process: dripped drop-by-drop through 10 feet of sugar maple charcoal prior to aging; column and pot doubler distilled with Cave Spring water
servingSuggestion: Jack & Coke or neat over rocks
whyWeCarry: We carry Jack Daniel's Old No. 7 because it is the most recognizable American whiskey in the world. Dripped drop by drop through ten feet of sugar maple charcoal before barreling, it develops sweet caramel, ripe banana, and gentle charcoal smoke. It is an essential, timeless staple on any American back bar.
seanShort: Sugar maple charcoal mellowing creates the iconic Lynchburg signature.
notes: I get sweet caramel, banana bread, and toasted oak right away. Charcoal filtration gives it a signature softness that makes it effortless to mix.
